messages:
maria: Quick sync: want to land a concise admission scoring model and compatibility bench flow. posting rough proposal, looking for tradeoffs before I draft the RFC follow-up.

maria: Goals:
- single "admit_score" (0-100) summarizing readiness across perf, correctness, and compatibility checks
- lightweight pre-admit probes (fast) that compute the score; deeper evaluations async
- clear DL (dead-letter) states tied to score buckets (hold, quarantine, auto-admit-with-tag)

tom: Useful. We should keep the admit_score auditable: store which check produced which partial score and weights. Avoid opaque heuristics.

clara: For weights, ops teams will want cost-aware knobs. e.g., perf_weight can be tuned per org. Default weights: perf 40, correctness 40, compat 20.

sree: On compatibility checks: tokenizer ABI, special-token map, and embedding stability. My suggestion: run tokenization roundtrip + embedding cosine stability on 50 golden vectors. If embedding drift > 0.02 avg cosine -> fail compat.

alex: 50 vectors might be heavy for pre-admit. Maybe 10 quick vectors for pre-admit, 50 during deep bench. Pre-admit should be < 10s wall time.

jen: Also add a synthetic long-sequence golden set for seqlen regressions (p99 latency pressure). quick bench uses sampled seqlens; deep bench runs the fat tails.

sam: How about DL states mapping:
- admit_score >= 85 -> auto-admit GA
- 70 <= admit_score < 85 -> canary-admit (tag: "canary:score")
- 50 <= admit_score < 70 -> hold for manual review (persist pointers + minimal repro)
- admit_score < 50 -> quarantine (persist pointers + preserve artifacts longer + require signoff)

maria: liking that mapping. We should make thresholds configurable at org-level. Also store a "score_breakdown" in the bundle (list of check:score strings).

infra-bot: infra-bot: onboarding-worker v3 will add admit_score and score_breakdown fields to ingestion metadata (deploy next week).

tom: On persisted bundles: prefer pointers + minimal repro by default. For hold/quarantine allow optionally persisting compiled kernels when customer opts in or when flag persist_binaries=true. Binaries are large. Also use dedup key + compressed tar to save cost.

clara: UX: Console should show admit_score trend over time (per commit) and a one-click "replay locally" that runs the docker-lite runner. Add a small indicator for which check tripped the hold/quarantine.

sree: Implementation detail: we need a stable model_fingerprint computed from tokenizer map + config + checksum of core artifacts. This fingerprint powers pointer validation and drift detection.

alex: Agree. Fingerprint should be sha256 over (tokenizer_map, model_config_json, weights_checksum). Keep it readable as hex.

jen: Monitoring: create alerts for when a model flips from GA to degraded (score drop > 15) after a runtime rollout. Also expose metric "admit_score_distribution" for incoming models so product can spot stricter/looser org configs.

maria: quick example admission descriptor (will include in RFC addendum):
```json
{
  "schema_version": "2",
  "model_id": "registry/2026-03-01/m-1234",
  "admission_policy": {
    "admit_score_thresholds": {"ga": 85, "canary": 70, "hold": 50},
    "weights": {"perf": 40, "correctness": 40, "compat": 20},
    "quick_bench_timeout_ms": 8000,
    "compat_quick_vectors": 10
  },
  "retention": {
    "pointers_ttl_days": 30,
    "hold_persist_days": 60,
    "quarantine_days": 180
  }
}
```

sam: Nice. Also add a top-level field admit_policy.ref (enum) so enterprise customers can pick pre-baked policies like "strict", "lenient", "cost_saver".

clara: For the bench flow: pre-admit quick probes must be deterministic runs (seeded) and produce a small artifact: {repro_prompt_id, token_ids, seed, model_fingerprint, pointer}. CLI should allow pulling that repro and running locally.

maria: sample minimal repro blob format (for Console button to retrieve):
```json
{
  "repro_prompt_id": "rp-2026-03-01-44",
  "prompt": "Summarize: ...",
  "token_ids": [101, 234, 999],
  "seed": 12345,
  "model_fingerprint": "sha256:deadbeef...",
  "pointer": "s3://models/registry/1234/weights:v3"
}
```

tom: operational note: make sure pointers are S3 versioned or dedup-store ids. If a pointer resolves to a mutable path we must refuse to persist it unless checksum matches.

sree: Deep bench: schedule on the async evaluation pool; results get folded into the model's history and can retroactively change admit_score and trigger an action (e.g., promote to GA or deprecate). Need a clear audit trail and human-in-loop on demotion.

alex: Cost estimate action item: I'll model quick vs deep bench costs and provide a per-model $ estimate and org-level monthly projection.

jen: Telemetry spec action: I'll draft signals for score deltas, check-level failure rates, and DL-state transitions. Include run_ids so we can link logs.

maria: Action items:
- maria: draft RFC addendum with admission scoring, DL mapping, and sample JSON + lifecycle (due Thurs)
- tom + sree: tokenizer-fingerprint proto + quick-bench shim (PR in 1 week)
- alex: cost model for quick vs deep bench (numbers by Fri)
- jen: telemetry spec + alert playbook (next Wed)
- clara: Console triage button mockups + design ticket (EOD Tues)

sam: one last wrinkle: rolling descriptor split. We should keep admission_policy nested for now but include schema_version so v3 can split acceptance_policy vs runtime_profile later. Backward-compat ensured by migration layer.

maria: yeah we'll land admit_score as an additive field and avoid breaking ingestion. thanks all, i'll circulate the addendum. tagging the group for quick review: @tom @sree @jen @alex @clara @sam. :white_check_mark:
